text:
alice: quick follow-up from the model-versioning RFC — can we sync on rollout metadata and pin semantics? want to lock compatibility checks before next deploy
ben: yes. two big open questions: what do we store as the canonical pin (semantic version vs immutable digest) and how strict are rollbacks? :thinking:
carmen: my vote: store both. model_ref (human), immutable_digest (sha256), and a compat_hash derived from tokenizer+spec. keeps human traceability + strictness for enforcement.
dylan: also need clear precedence: request override > route pin > org default. otherwise chaos when infra tries to auto-fallback.
elaine: +1. for rollback semantics: do NOT auto-unpin on failure. runtime should attempt a configured fallback list then mark a human-alert for manual rollback. auto-unpin is risky. :warning:
ben: what about compatibility levels? like input-level, runtime-level, or full-binary? runtime-level would check KV cache layout + attention kernel compat. cheaper checks first.
alice: agreed. propose an enum compat_level: NONE|INPUT|RUNTIME|BINARY. default RUNTIME.
carmen: example metadata sketch:```json
{
  "model_ref": "redwood/gptx-7b",
  "immutable_digest": "sha256:0b9c4f...",
  "pin_type": "hard",            // hard vs soft (soft allows transparent fallback)
  "compat_hash": "sha256:9f3a2e...",
  "compat_level": "RUNTIME",
  "fallbacks": ["redwood/gptx-7b-quant", "redwood/gptx-6.9b"],
  "schema_version": "v2"
}
```
ben: looks good. we should document what goes into compat_hash. tokenizer config + vocab id + KV cache format + model config version. that should catch breaking tokenization or cache layout changes.
dylan: runtime note: if compat_level >= RUNTIME we should run a cheap header-compare on startup for cached models to fail fast.
elaine: telemetry: include fields for pin_applied_ts, pin_source (api/console/cli), and rollout_id so we can trace regressions. also add an optional "approval_ticket" field for enterprise workflows.
aIice: tiny nit: name collision risk between "schema_version" and runtime kernel schema. prefer rollout_schema_version.
carmen: good catch. rename in the example to rollout_schema_version.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for rollout_id=rl_2026_0421_11, targets=service/*, pinned=redwood/gptx-7b@sha256:0b9c4f..., mode=soft
ben: ops question: will Dedicated/Private tenants be allowed to opt into relaxed compat checks? some enterprise customers will want control.
dylan: yes — add tenant_override boolean and a policy_url reference. we already have the policy engine to gate it.
elaine: action items: alice create small RFC addendum with the compat_level enum + compat_hash definition. ben to spec the compat_hash generation. carmen to update example metadata and CLI flags. dylan to prototype header-compare check in runtime. i'll add telemetry fields and enterprise flags.
alice: thanks. i'll draft the addendum today and tag you all. :thumbsup:
ben: ping me on the draft, i'll review.
carmen: dropping a note to the repo with the example and tests.
dylan: will open a runtime PR for the startup check.
elaine: will add telemetry + docs PR for enterprise controls.
deploy-bot: canary 50% -> success, 5/5 hosts healthy, rolling to 100% in 10m
